findings.text: DATA MODEL: users table requires profile_image_url VARCHAR(2048) NULLABLE, profile_image_updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULLABLE. Index: btree on (id) already primary key — no additional index needed for single-row lookups. Constraint: profile_image_url must match pattern '^https://[a-z0-9.-]+\.amazonaws\.com/' when non-null (enforced at DB check constraint level). No separate profile_images table is warranted for single-image-per-user semantics; adding a column is the minimal change that satisfies AC-3 and AC-4.

API ENDPOINTS (3 routes, all require authenticated session — Bearer token / session cookie): (1) POST /users/{userId}/profile-image — multipart/form-data, field name 'image', returns 200 {profile_image_url}. (2) DELETE /users/{userId}/profile-image — no body, returns 204 on success. (3) GET /users/{userId}/profile-image — returns 200 {profile_image_url, profile_image_updated_at} or 404 if none set. All routes enforce: caller's authenticated userId == path userId (no cross-user access). S3 key pattern: users/{userId}/profile.{ext}.

ERROR HANDLING MATRIX: (a) Format invalid (not JPG/PNG) → 422 {code:'INVALID_FORMAT', allowed:['image/jpeg','image/png']}. (b) Size >5MB → 422 {code:'FILE_TOO_LARGE', limit_bytes:5242880}. (c) Dimensions <100x100 → 422 {code:'DIMENSIONS_TOO_SMALL', minimum:100}. (d) MIME/extension mismatch (magic bytes differ from extension) → 422 {code:'MIME_MISMATCH'}. (e) S3 upload fails → 502 {code:'STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE'}; no DB write attempted. (f) S3 succeeds but DB update fails → 502 {code:'DB_UPDATE_FAILED'}; compensating S3 delete issued asynchronously; client retries are safe (idempotent key = userId). (g) S3 delete fails on replace → 202 accepted but orphan logged for async cleanup job. (h) Unauthenticated → 401. (i) Authenticated but wrong userId → 403. (j) User not found → 404.

DATABASE TRANSACTION PATTERN: Atomic update on POST uses single UPDATE users SET profile_image_url = $1, profile_image_updated_at = NOW() WHERE id = $2 inside a serializable transaction. Old S3 key is read BEFORE the transaction begins (SELECT profile_image_url FROM users WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE). Sequence: (1) SELECT FOR UPDATE old URL, (2) upload new file to S3, (3) UPDATE users row, (4) COMMIT, (5) async delete old S3 object. If step 3 or 4 fails, step 5 is skipped; compensating delete of the newly-uploaded S3 object is issued. Row-level lock on step 1 prevents concurrent upload race for the same userId.

TEST SCENARIOS — happy path: (T1) Upload valid JPG 200x200 2MB → 200, DB updated, old S3 object deleted. (T2) Upload replaces existing image → only one S3 object per user after completion. (T3) GET after upload → returns correct URL. (T4) DELETE after upload → 204, DB url null, S3 object deleted. (T5) GET after delete → 404.

TEST SCENARIOS — validation failures: (T6) Upload BMP file → 422 INVALID_FORMAT. (T7) Upload 6MB JPG → 422 FILE_TOO_LARGE. (T8) Upload 50x50 PNG → 422 DIMENSIONS_TOO_SMALL. (T9) Upload file with .jpg extension but PNG magic bytes → 422 MIME_MISMATCH. (T10) POST with no file field → 422 missing required field. (T11) PUT (wrong method) → 405.

TEST SCENARIOS — infrastructure failures: (T12) S3 upload times out → 502 STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, DB unchanged, no orphan created. (T13) S3 succeeds, DB update fails (simulated constraint violation) → 502 DB_UPDATE_FAILED, compensating S3 delete enqueued; retry by client uploads same file and succeeds. (T14) Concurrent uploads for same userId: second request acquires FOR UPDATE lock and waits; first completes; second then proceeds — only one final S3 object. (T15) DELETE when no image set → 204 (idempotent, no error).

PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS: Upload request timeout = 30 seconds server-side (client surfaces progress for >2s uploads per AC open question OPEN-1, left to architect). Max concurrent uploads per user = 1 (enforced by DB row-level lock, not rate limiter). Max concurrent uploads globally = platform-default connection pool limit (no additional cap specified; architect to confirm). Storage limit per user = 5MB enforced at validation layer; no per-account storage quota beyond single-file constraint. S3 presigned URL expiry for GET reads = 3600 seconds (1 hour); configurable via environment variable S3_URL_EXPIRY_SECONDS.

SECURITY: (1) Access control — authenticated caller's userId from JWT/session must equal path {userId}; no admin override path defined in this story. (2) Input validation — MIME magic-byte check (not extension-only) mandatory to prevent polyglot file attacks. (3) S3 — bucket ACL private; all reads via presigned URLs only; no public-read objects. (4) CSRF — POST /profile-image is a state-mutating endpoint; Web clients must include CSRF token in header (X-CSRF-Token). Mobile clients use Bearer token which is inherently CSRF-safe. (5) PII note — profile image URL is not PII per se but links to user identity; treat as internal data; do not expose in unauthenticated responses. (6) No payment data involved; G-10 CJIS gate is not triggered by this story.

PLATFORM FLOWS: iOS — UIImagePickerController or PHPickerViewController; compress to JPEG quality 0.8 before upload if source is HEIC; send as multipart/form-data over HTTPS; disable upload button on submit, re-enable on response. Android — Intent.ACTION_GET_CONTENT with image/* MIME filter; decode Bitmap to check dimensions before upload; send multipart via OkHttp or Retrofit; show progress indicator. Web — drag-drop zone (ondrop) + <input type='file' accept='image/jpeg,image/png'>; read File object, check size/dimensions client-side before POST; show progress via XHR onprogress or fetch with ReadableStream. All platforms: validate format, size, dimensions client-side first (fast fail UX), then re-validate server-side (authoritative).

OPEN — Image resizing: AC-2 requires >=100x100 minimum but does not specify whether the server resizes images to a canonical size (e.g. 256x256) or stores originals up to 5MB. Two interpretations: (A) store original, no resize; (B) resize to 256x256 on ingest, discard original. Impacts S3 storage costs and CDN caching. PO decision required before architect finalises storage pipeline. This finding carries forward from phase-1 OPEN-1 (partial).

OPEN — S3 region/bucket/CDN: Phase 1 OPEN-1 deferred S3 region, bucket name, and CDN strategy. Architect must decide before implementation: (A) same-region bucket as application servers (latency optimised); (B) CloudFront CDN in front of S3 (presigned URL strategy changes). Presigned URL generation differs materially between the two. This is a BLOCKING dependency for the software-engineer phase if unresolved.

OPEN — Soft delete vs permanent deletion: AC-5 says 'delete profile image' but does not specify whether the S3 object and DB record are permanently erased or soft-deleted (url nulled, S3 object retained for N days). Two interpretations: (A) permanent delete — S3 object deleted immediately, DB column set null; (B) soft delete — DB column nulled, S3 object moved to archive prefix for 30 days. PO must clarify before implementation. Defaulting to (A) permanent delete unless PO responds; architect records assumption.

decisions: Phase 2 elaborates phase 1 intake into full functional specification; no new ACs introduced; all 7 original ACs addressed.
Data model: single column addition (profile_image_url, profile_image_updated_at) to users table; no new table; coordinator with solution architect required before DB migration is written.
API design: 3 RESTful endpoints (POST/DELETE/GET) on /users/{userId}/profile-image; all require authenticated session; cross-user access blocked at authorization layer.
Transaction pattern: SELECT FOR UPDATE → S3 upload → DB UPDATE → COMMIT → async old-object delete; compensating rollback on S3 success + DB failure.
Security posture: private S3 ACL + presigned URLs; MIME magic-byte validation; CSRF token on web; no CJIS patterns involved (G-10 not triggered).
Three open questions (OPEN-2 image resizing, OPEN-3 S3/CDN strategy, OPEN-4 soft vs hard delete) carried forward as MEDIUM OPEN findings; OPEN-3 is BLOCKING for software-engineer phase if unresolved.
Performance: 30s server timeout, single concurrent upload per user via row lock, 5MB hard limit at validation, S3 presigned URL TTL 3600s configurable.
Platform notes: iOS HEIC→JPEG conversion before upload; Android Bitmap decode for dimension check; Web client-side pre-validation + server authoritative re-validation.
blockers: OPEN-3 (S3 region/bucket/CDN strategy) is a BLOCKING dependency for phase 5 (software-engineer). Solution architect must resolve before implementation begins. It is not blocking phase 3 (ui-designer) or phase 4 (solution-architect) — the architect phase is the correct resolution point.
